name: atomic-index-promotion
explain: Use a real SQLite transaction to show that a failed publication cannot leave a changed active pointer. Candidate validation is represented by an injected exception; external vector durability is outside this fixture.
steps: Roll back a pointer update after a validation failure. || Commit a guarded promotion and verify the active generation.

name: ingestion-contract-fingerprint
expect: key order: stable; model change: rebuild
explain: Compute a canonical configuration digest. The fixture checks key-order stability and a representation-changing model revision; it does not identify actual provider revisions.
steps: Serialize the full representation contract deterministically. || Compare a key reorder and an actual model revision change.

name: job-claim-arbitration
expect: A owns job; B must skip
explain: Execute a real guarded SQL transition twice to isolate the ownership predicate. The local sequential schedule does not test database lock timing or PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED.
steps: Commit the first eligible ownership transition. || Reject the second claimant after its predicate no longer matches.

name: fenced-job-completion
expect: stale rejected; current completed; duplicate ignored
explain: Validate current ownership and attempt generation in the same SQL write that marks completion. External effect fencing requires a corresponding destination design.
steps: Reject the old owner and generation. || Accept the current attempt exactly once at the guarded transition.

name: idempotency-publication-window
explain: Compare two explicitly ordered schedules to demonstrate a publication gap. This fixture makes no distributed atomicity or external-effect claim.
steps: Release first and observe the second worker can start. || Publish first and observe retries can replay even after release.

name: degraded-idempotency-admission
expect: reads proceed; unprotected writes defer; destination-dedup writes proceed
explain: Exercise an explicit admission policy. Coordination alone still needs effect reconciliation; the example intentionally makes that requirement visible in its return value.
steps: Classify reads separately from writes. || Admit degraded writes only with the declared durable protection.

name: complete-procedure-manifest
expect: complete accepted; missing, duplicate and reordered steps rejected
explain: Validate exact step order and version. A production manifest should additionally verify content digests, authorization and graph edges where applicable.
steps: Accept the full ordered version. || Reject missing, duplicated or reordered required steps.

name: pinned-procedure-revocation
expect: pinned v3 retained for audit; execution blocked
explain: Demonstrate version pinning with an independent revocation check. Approval migration and durable persistence require additional application rules.
steps: Read the immutable task version. || Apply current revocation policy before resolving the next permitted action.

name: stream-durability-terminal
expect: unsaved draft != durable answer; saved answer != successful effect
explain: Model distinct outcome fields so a fluent answer cannot accidentally imply durable storage or business success. This is an application contract fixture, not a live SSE test.
steps: Represent generated-but-unsaved output explicitly. || Preserve failed business outcome even when its explanatory message was saved.

name: feedback-answer-identity
expect: one updated rating; foreign answer rejected
explain: Illustrate owner checks and updating one current rating. A production endpoint needs transactional uniqueness, authentication and answer-revision provenance.
steps: Validate target ownership before accepting feedback. || Update the current rating and reject a foreign-message attempt.

name: evaluation-mode-provenance
expect: proxy rejected; compatible live evidence accepted
explain: Require execution provenance before considering a synthetic score. The example validates report routing, not model accuracy.
steps: Reject a high score produced by the wrong system. || Accept compatible live-mode provenance only after applying the score threshold.

name: abstention-subset-denominators
expect: correct abstention: 1.0; false refusal: 1.0; gate: fail
explain: Compute explicit subset rates and show that always refusing fails the combined gate. The fixture does not judge natural-language refusals.
steps: Separate answerable and unanswerable denominators. || Reject an always-refuse policy and mark empty populations unmeasured.

name: hybrid-missing-distance
expect: zero preserved; missing preserved; channel ranks fused separately
explain: Preserve metric absence through JSON and keep synthetic rank fusion separate from raw distances. The ranks are fixtures, not a retrieval benchmark.
steps: Round-trip zero and missing values without truthiness defaults. || Fuse per-channel ranks into a separate score.

name: retrieval-invariant-regression
expect: valid rank swaps pass; missing or forbidden evidence fails
explain: Check evidence-set coverage and exclusions without freezing harmless rank swaps. This is a labeled-fixture contract, not a provider search test.
steps: Accept either valid ordering of both required sources. || Reject missing support or an ineligible candidate.

name: transactional-notification-intent
expect: business change rolled back; notification intent rolled back
explain: Execute and roll back two related database writes in one real transaction. Notification-provider delivery is deliberately outside this local fixture.
steps: Write the business transition and outbox event together. || Inject failure and verify that neither survives rollback.

name: notification-destination-dedup
expect: lost acknowledgment replay: one feed item
explain: Use a real SQLite uniqueness constraint to absorb repeated delivery of one logical event. External channels require their own verified idempotency contracts.
steps: Commit the first feed item under a stable event identity. || Replay after a lost acknowledgment and verify the destination remains singular.
